nodes.name: Fe-doped Ni(OH)2 nanosheets on Ni foam

properties.description: Iron-doped nickel hydroxide on Ni foam

nodes.name: Ni foam surface activation
nodes.procedure: Typically, a piece of Ni Foam (5 cm × 2.5 cm) was immersed in HCl solution (3 M, 100 mL) at 90 °C for 20 min to activate the surface of Ni foam. Then the activated Ni foam was stored in a beaker with a preservative film for 3 h.
nodes.source_text: a piece of Ni Foam (5 cm × 2.5 cm) was immersed in HCl solution (3 M, 100 mL) at 90 °C for 20 min to activate the surface of Ni foam. Then the activated Ni foam was stored in a beaker with a preservative film for 3 h.

nodes.name: Autologous Ni(OH)2 growth
nodes.procedure: After that, the Ni foam was taken out and immersed in prepared NaOH (1 M) and K2S2O8 (0.3 M) mixed solution for 3 h at room temperature to obtain Ni(OH)2 nanosheets on Ni foam (Ni(OH)2/Ni). Then, the Ni(OH)2/Ni was cleaned with deionized water for several times.

unit_operations.procedure_snippet: immersed in prepared NaOH (1 M) and K2S2O8 (0.3 M) mixed solution for 3 h at room temperature

nodes.source_text: the Ni foam was taken out and immersed in prepared NaOH (1 M) and K2S2O8 (0.3 M) mixed solution for 3 h at room temperature to obtain Ni(OH)2 nanosheets on Ni foam (Ni(OH)2/Ni). Then, the Ni(OH)2/Ni was cleaned with deionized water for several times.

nodes.name: Fe electrochemical doping
nodes.procedure: The FeeNieOH nanosheet arrays were then synthesized by in situ electrochemical-assisted doping Fe into Ni(OH)2 in 0.1 M (NH4)2Fe(SO4)2 at a current density of 1 mA cm^-2 for 1200 s.
nodes.source_text: The FeeNieOH nanosheet arrays were then synthesized by in situ electrochemical-assisted doping Fe into Ni(OH)2 in 0.1 M (NH4)2Fe(SO4)2 at a current density of 1 mA cm^-2 for 1200 s.

nodes.description: OER performance in O₂-saturated 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The total OER activity was first determined by linear sweep voltammetry (LSV) with a small scan rate of 2 mV s⁻¹ in an O₂-saturated KOH (1 M) solution... The FeeNieOH requires an overpotential of 220 mV to reach the current density of 10 mA cm⁻²... 500 mA cm⁻² with a low overpotential of 290 mV. FeeNieOH exhibited the smallest Tafel slope of 48.3 mV dec⁻¹

nodes.description: OER long-term stability in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The OER stability tests of the FeeNieOH electrode were conducted by galvanostatic measurements (50 mA cm⁻², 100 mA cm⁻² and 500 mA cm⁻²,) for 24 h and multi-step galvanostatic... under a large current density of 500 mA cm⁻² for 600 h

nodes.description: Overall water splitting in 1 M KOH (bifunctional)
nodes.source_text: Using the FeeNieOH electrode as anode and cathode for overall water splitting, only a small overpotential of 1.57 V is required to reach a current density of 10 mA cm⁻²... long-term stability measurements were also conducted under constant current densities of 100 and 500 mA cm⁻² in 1 M KOH for 20 h

nodes.description: OER LSV comparison in O₂-saturated 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The OER activity of FeeNieOH was evaluated in 1 M KOH solution. For comparison, the LSV curves of Ni(OH)₂/Ni and bare Ni electrode were also conducted under the same condition.

Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) was performed at an overpotential of 0.27 V in a frequency range between 0.1 Hz and 100 kHz at an amplitude of 10 mV... The R_ct value of the FeeNieOH (1.72 Ω)

The double-layer capacitance (C_dl) was obtained from cyclic voltammetry (CV) curves with different scan rates (10 mV s⁻¹ - 100 mV s⁻¹), across a potential range from 1.03 V to 1.13 V. The calculated value of the FeeNieOH electrode is about 3.52 mF cm⁻²

nodes.description: OER LSV and EIS comparison in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: As shown in Fig. 3a, the bare Ni foam exhibits negligible OER activity

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show Ni(OH)₂/Ni and FeeNieOH/Ni both exhibit ultrathin nanosheets with porous structure; FeeNieOH maintains morphology after Fe doping with more and wider intervals.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 2a and b are scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images of the autologous growth of NieOH ultrathin nanosheets, which show the porous structure with numerous small intervals. After electrochemical-assisted Fe substitution (Fig. 2c and d), the morphology of FeeNieOH perfectly maintains ultrathin nanosheets with porous architectures...

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM image confirms porous architecture of FeeNieOH nanosheets scratched from Ni foam; EDX mapping shows uniform Fe distribution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) was used to further investigate the morphology of FeeNieOH nanosheets that had been scratched from Ni foam, which further confirms the porous architecture of FeeNieOH... the EDX mapping demonstrates that the Fe element is uniformly distributed throughout the network.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM-EDS elemental mapping shows uniform distribution of Fe, Ni, O in FeeNieOH confirming successful Fe doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: To further investigate the distribution of the FeeNieOH, the SEM equipped energy X-ray dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) was conducted (Fig. S4). The elemental mapping results disclose the uniform distribution of the Fe, Ni, and O...

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows peaks at 2θ = 19.21°, 33.13°, 38.69°, 59.21° and 62.74° assigned to hexagonal β-Ni(OH)₂ (PDF#14-0117); Fe incorporation maintains similar peak positions with lower intensity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2g, the three intense peaks, marked by *, correspond to the Ni substrate, while the peaks at 2θ = 19.21°, 33.13°, 38.69°, 59.21° and 62.74° can be assigned to the hexagonal β-Ni(OH)₂ (PDF#14e0117).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman bands at 480 and 551 cm⁻¹ attributed to Ni-O vibrations in oxyhydroxide nickel.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The pair of bands at 480 and 551 cm⁻¹ are attributed to NieO vibrations in oxyhydroxide nickel, whose results are similar to XRD.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows Ni 2p₃/₂ at 855.88 eV (Ni²⁺) for both Ni(OH)₂ and FeeNieOH; Fe 2p₃/₂ at 712.20 eV and 2p₁/₂ at 725.20 eV confirm Fe³⁺ in FeeNieOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2h, the singlet peak at 855.88 eV with a satellite peak is assigned to Ni 2p₃/₂... The high-resolution of the Fe 2p spectrum is shown in Fig. 2i. The peaks at 712.20 and 725.20 eV are attributed to the Fe 2p₃/₂ and Fe 2p₁/₂ regions...

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ adsorption-desorption isotherms measured; specific surface area of Ni(OH)₂ close to FeeNieOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The N₂ adsorption-desorption isotherms of the electrodes were measured at 77 K... and the specific surface area was calculated using the BrunauereEmmetteTeller (BET).

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at different scan rates gives Cdl = 3.52 mF cm⁻² for FeeNieOH, 3.97 mF cm⁻² for Ni(OH)₂/Ni, and 1.07 mF cm⁻² for bare Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The calculated value of the FeeNieOH electrode is about 3.52 mF cm⁻², which is higher than that of bare Ni (1.07 mF cm⁻²) but slightly inferior to Ni(OH)₂ electrode (3.97 mF cm⁻²).

nodes.characterization_summary: Rct of FeeNieOH is 1.72 Ω, 6.8 times smaller than bare Ni and 1.3 times smaller than Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Rct value of the FeeNieOH (1.72 Ω) is about 6.8 times and 1.3 times smaller than that of the bare Ni and Ni(OH)₂ electrodes.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-stability test XPS shows Ni 2p peak at 855.75 eV similar to initial 855.88 eV; Fe 2p spectra remain similar.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 4d, the initial peak at 855.88 eV is close to the peaks after the long-term stability test (855.75 eV). The high-resolution XPS spectra of Fe 2p is also highly similar to initial ones.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-stability test XRD patterns of FeeNieOH/Ni match initial patterns, confirming unchanged crystal phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fig. 4c shows the XRD patterns of FeeNieOH/Ni electrodes after the test, which match well with the initial ones, suggesting the unchanged crystal phase.

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-stability test SEM shows FeeNieOH/Ni retains porous ultrathin nanosheet architecture.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FeeNieOH/Ni electrodes retain the porous architecture of previous ultrathin nanosheets (Fig. S11).

nodes.characterization_summary: Post-stability test EDS mapping confirms uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, O elements in FeeNieOH/Ni.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS mapping images demonstrate the uniform distribution of Ni, Fe and O elements (Fig. S12).
